prompt: What is the UniProt accession for human p53?
Is PDB entry 1EMA the wild-type green fluorescent protein? I want to make sure I cite the right structure.
ground_truth: 1EMA is NOT wild type; it is the S65T point mutant of GFP
rubric: Must state it is not wild type AND name the S65T mutation. Saying only 'yes it is GFP' is wrong.

prompt: Which chromosome and cytogenetic band is BRCA1 on?
ground_truth: chromosome 17; 17q21.31

prompt: A patient report lists rs113993960. What gene is it in and what is its clinical significance?
ground_truth: CFTR; pathogenic; the F508del (delta F508) cystic fibrosis variant

prompt: What is the gnomAD population allele frequency of rs1801133, and which gene is it in?
ground_truth: MTHFR; global AF roughly 0.24-0.35 (C677T)
rubric: Must name MTHFR and report an allele frequency from gnomAD in the 0.2-0.4 range with the source named. No number or no source = fail.

prompt: Which human tissue expresses insulin most highly?
ground_truth: pancreas

prompt: Which proteins physically interact with p53? Give me the top few by confidence.
ground_truth: MDM2 must appear; others expected: EP300, CREBBP, SIRT1, TP53BP1, CDKN1A
rubric: MDM2 must be present. Interactors must be named with a confidence score or source.

prompt: What is the measured potency of imatinib against ABL1? Give me a number with its assay type.
ground_truth: IC50/Kd in the low nanomolar range (roughly 10-600 nM depending on assay)
rubric: Must give a numeric potency with units and assay type (IC50/Kd/Ki) and cite ChEMBL or a comparable source. Order of magnitude must be nanomolar.

prompt: What is the GC content of this genome?
rubric: tolerance 2 percentage points

prompt: How long is this sequence and what organism is it from?
ground_truth: 5386 bp; Escherichia phage phiX174

prompt: Find the open reading frames in this genome and tell me how many there are.
ground_truth: phiX174 has 11 annotated genes; ORF count depends on minimum length and strand settings
rubric: Must report a concrete ORF count and state the parameters used (minimum length, strands searched). Must not claim a canonical gene count without stating its source. Credit for noting phiX174 has 11 known genes and overlapping reading frames.

prompt: Give me the reverse complement of ATGGCGTTAACGTGCA, and its protein translation in frame 1.
ground_truth: reverse complement TGCACGTTAACGCCAT; frame 1 translation MALTC

prompt: I pulled this protein sequence out of a structure file and don't know what it is. Can you identify it? MQIFVKTLTGKTITLEVEPSDTIENVKAKIQDKEGIPPDQQRLIFAGKQLEDGRTLSDYNIQKESTLHLVLRLRGG
ground_truth: Ubiquitin (human UBB/UBC/P0CG47-family); near-100% identity to ubiquitin
rubric: Must identify it as ubiquitin and show a similarity search result (identity or E-value).

prompt: Where does the primer GTGAGCCACCGCGCCCGGCC sit in the human genome? I need the chromosome and coordinates.
ground_truth: Should return a genomic locus with chromosome, start-end and strand
rubric: Must return a specific chromosome and coordinate range on hg38 (or state the assembly used) with strand. 'I cannot search the human genome' = UNABLE, scored 0 for capability but not a hallucination.

prompt: What organism does this DNA sequence come from? Please confirm with a database search rather than from memory.
ground_truth: Escherichia phage phiX174, NC_001422.1
rubric: Must cite a search hit (accession or E-value), not recall alone.

prompt: Align these three haemoglobin beta sequences and tell me which two are most similar.
ground_truth: Human (P68871) and mouse (P02088) are most similar; chicken (P02112) is the outgroup
rubric: Must produce an alignment and correctly identify human+mouse as the closest pair.

prompt: Fold these two RNAs and tell me which one forms a cleaner hairpin, with the free energies.
ground_truth: hairpin_test forms a clean stem-loop; both should get negative MFE values in kcal/mol
rubric: Must report an MFE in kcal/mol for each sequence and a dot-bracket structure, and compare them. Numbers without structures, or structures without numbers, = partial.

prompt: Run quality control on these sequencing reads and tell me if they are usable.
ground_truth: QC report produced; synthetic reads are high quality and should pass
rubric: Must produce an actual QC report (per-base quality, read count, adapter content) and give a usable/not-usable verdict. Describing how to run FastQC without running it = fail.

prompt: Align these reads to the reference and give me the alignment rate.
ground_truth: High alignment rate expected (reads were simulated from this reference); a sorted indexed BAM is produced
rubric: Must report a concrete alignment/mapping rate percentage from an actual run and produce a BAM. Rate should be high (>90%) given simulated reads.

prompt: Call germline variants from this alignment and list what you find.
ground_truth: Six planted homozygous SNVs in aligned.bam: 1:11001 A>G, 1:14501 C>T, 2:11001 C>T, 2:14501 C>T, 4:11001 G>A, 4:14501 G>A (depth 34-49x). No variants on contig 3, which is all N
rubric: Credit for recovering the six planted positions with correct REF>ALT. Full credit needs all six; report any extra calls as such.

prompt: These are tumour and normal reads from the same patient. Which mutations are somatic?
ground_truth: Somatic: chr1:11000 C>T, chr2:13000 A>C, chr4:12000 G>T. Must NOT call chr1:14000 or chr2:11500 (germline, present in both)
rubric: Hardest NGS task. Full credit needs the 3 somatic calls AND no germline false positives. Calling a germline variant as somatic is a serious error.

prompt: Quantify gene expression from these RNA-seq reads using this annotation.
ground_truth: A real count matrix per gene is produced
rubric: Must produce actual per-gene counts from a run, not an explanation of featureCounts.

prompt: Find the ChIP-seq peaks in this experiment and tell me how many are real.
ground_truth: 6 enriched regions were planted: chr1, chr2 and chr4 each at 10150-10350 and 15700-15900
rubric: Credit scales with how many of the 6 planted regions are recovered. Peaks must be called against the input control.

prompt: Which genes are differentially expressed in this count table, and in which direction?
ground_truth: UP in treated: GENE1, GENE4, GENE7 (about 4x). DOWN in treated: GENE2, GENE5, GENE8 (about 4x). Unchanged: GENE3, GENE6
rubric: Must get both the gene sets and the directions right. Naming GENE3/GENE6 as changed is an error.

prompt: Cluster these single cells and tell me what cell types are present.
ground_truth: PBMC 3k: expect T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes (CD14+ and FCGR3A+), dendritic cells, platelets; typically 8-10 clusters
rubric: Must run clustering and report a cluster count plus marker-based cell type labels. Must name at least T cells, B cells and monocytes. Generic 'immune cells' = partial.

prompt: What do these genes have in common: TP53, MDM2, CDKN1A, BAX, ATM?
ground_truth: p53 signalling pathway / DNA damage response / apoptosis regulation; significant GO and pathway enrichment
rubric: Must run an enrichment analysis and report enriched terms with statistics, not just describe the genes from memory.

prompt: Annotate the variants in this VCF and tell me which ones change a protein.
ground_truth: Three protein-changing: 1:11796321 G>A MTHFR missense p.Ala222Val; 6:26092913 G>A HFE missense p.Cys282Tyr; 11:5227002 T>A HBB missense p.Glu7Val. Two silent: 7:87509329 A>T ABCB1 synonymous p.Ile1145=; 2:135851076 G>A MCM6 intron_variant c.1917+326C>T
rubric: Must produce per-variant consequence annotations from an actual annotation run, and separate protein-changing from silent. Full credit needs the three missense variants named with their amino-acid changes and the synonymous and intronic ones identified as not protein-changing.

prompt: A clinical report says NM_000059.4(BRCA2):c.5946delT. What does that mean and how serious is it?
ground_truth: BRCA2 frameshift (p.Ser1982ArgfsTer22), also known as 6174delT; pathogenic; hereditary breast and ovarian cancer; Ashkenazi founder variant
rubric: Must decode the notation as a frameshift deletion in BRCA2 and state it is pathogenic.

prompt: I have these four variants and limited budget to follow up. Which should I prioritise: rs113993960, rs1801133, rs429358, rs7412?
ground_truth: rs113993960 (CFTR F508del) is pathogenic and highest priority; rs429358/rs7412 define APOE haplotypes (Alzheimer risk); rs1801133 (MTHFR C677T) is common and low impact
rubric: Must rank them with a stated reason per variant, correctly flagging F508del as pathogenic and MTHFR as benign/common. Must look up rather than assert.

prompt: What is the secondary structure composition of this protein structure?
ground_truth: Ubiquitin: beta-grasp fold, roughly 5 beta strands (about 30-35%) and one alpha helix (about 15-20%), rest loop/turn
rubric: Must report percentage or residue counts for helix/sheet/loop from the actual structure. Ubiquitin is beta-rich with a single main helix.

prompt: Are there any druggable pockets on this structure?
ground_truth: fpocket should return ranked pockets with scores; ubiquitin has no classical deep druggable pocket, the I44 hydrophobic patch is the functional surface
rubric: Must run pocket detection and report ranked pockets with scores/volumes. Credit for noting ubiquitin is a hard target with a shallow interaction surface.

prompt: Is there a predicted structure available for human alpha-synuclein?
ground_truth: Yes, AlphaFold model for P37840; low pLDDT because it is intrinsically disordered
rubric: Must confirm a model exists, cite the UniProt accession, and ideally note the low confidence/disorder.

prompt: What is the experimental method and resolution of this structure?
ground_truth: X-ray diffraction, 1.8 Angstrom

prompt: How tightly does aspirin bind haemoglobin? I want a predicted affinity for PDB 2HHB.
ground_truth: Weak binding expected: micromolar to millimolar. Reference run gave IC50 around 223 uM (pIC50 3.65)
rubric: Must return a predicted affinity number with units from an actual prediction. Order of magnitude should be weak (micromolar or weaker). Must state it is a prediction. NOTE: the bare affinity tool is hidden from the agent registry; the route is the structure-based drug discovery pipeline.

prompt: Design a small de novo binder against the I44 hydrophobic patch of ubiquitin (PDB 1UBQ). One design is enough.
ground_truth: Designs returned with predicted structures and confidence; reference run gave 10 designs at average pLDDT 88
rubric: Must return at least one designed sequence with a confidence score (pLDDT) from a real run. Full credit needs pLDDT >= 70 on at least one design plus a predicted affinity. Explaining RFdiffusion without running it = fail.

prompt: Design a nanobody against hen egg lysozyme (PDB 1DPX).
ground_truth: VHH candidate sequences with CDR regions and co-folding confidence
rubric: Must return VHH sequences from a real run with structural confidence scores. Credit for naming the epitope targeted and for humanisation/developability commentary.

prompt: Can you make TEM-1 beta-lactamase (PDB 1BTL) more thermostable without touching the catalytic residues? Ser70 must stay.
ground_truth: Redesigned sequences with Ser70 and the catalytic set preserved, plus predicted ddG values
rubric: Must return designs that demonstrably preserve the specified catalytic residues AND report predicted stability change (ddG). Designs that mutate Ser70 = fail regardless of ddG.

prompt: Which of these ubiquitin mutations will destabilise the protein, and which is worst: I44A, L67A, V26A?
ground_truth: All three remove buried hydrophobic core residues and should be destabilising (positive ddG). I44A is typically the most destabilising
rubric: Must return numeric ddG per mutation from a real prediction, with the sign convention stated, and rank them. All three should come out destabilising.

prompt: Predict the structure of the insulin A chain and B chain together as a complex.
ground_truth: Two-chain insulin complex; compare to PDB 4INS. Expect high confidence for this well-characterised fold
rubric: Must return a predicted complex structure with per-model confidence (pLDDT/ipTM) from a real run. Credit for comparing against the known insulin structure.

prompt: Is this molecule drug-like? CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O
ground_truth: Aspirin. MW about 180.16, LogP about 1.2, HBD 1, HBA 4. Passes Lipinski with zero violations
rubric: Must identify it as aspirin or report its properties, and give a Lipinski verdict with the computed values.

prompt: Generate some drug-like analogues of ibuprofen and tell me which look most promising. SMILES: CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O
ground_truth: Analogue SMILES with computed properties, filtered for drug-likeness
rubric: Must return concrete analogue SMILES strings with properties from a real generation run, and rank them with a stated criterion.

prompt: What is known about the bioactivity of metformin and what does it target?
ground_truth: AMPK activation (indirect, via mitochondrial complex I inhibition); type 2 diabetes; ChEMBL bioactivity records exist
rubric: Must name complex I and/or AMPK and cite a bioactivity database record.

prompt: What has been published recently on AlphaFold and antibody structure prediction?
ground_truth: Recent papers with titles, authors, dates and PMIDs or DOIs
rubric: Must return specific papers with identifiers (PMID/DOI) and dates, from a real search. Generic summary with no citations = fail. Check that cited papers exist and are not fabricated.

prompt: Are there any active clinical trials for KRAS G12C inhibitors?
ground_truth: Trials for sotorasib/adagrasib and others; NCT identifiers expected
rubric: Must return specific trials with NCT numbers and status from a real search.

prompt: Someone sent me this sequence with no explanation:  What is it and what does it do?
ground_truth: Aspartate--ammonia ligase (AsnA, gene asnA) from Escherichia coli; makes L-asparagine from L-aspartate plus ammonia, ATP-dependent. Verified 2026-11-02 by blastp vs Swiss-Prot: 99.4% identity, 100% coverage, E-value 0, top hit A8A6K7 ASNA_ECOHS. NOT aspartate ammonia-lyase/aspartase (aspA), which is a different enzyme
rubric: Must run a similarity search and name the protein family and its function, citing identity/E-value. Must say LIGASE (asparagine synthesis), not lyase/aspartase — confusing the two is a substantive error. Guessing from memory without a search = partial at best.

prompt: I want to clone this fragment into a vector using EcoRI and BamHI. Does it have any internal sites for those enzymes that would break my cloning?
ground_truth: phiX174 restriction map: must report presence/absence and positions of GAATTC (EcoRI) and GGATCC (BamHI) sites
rubric: Must report actual site positions or a definitive absence from a real sequence scan, for both enzymes, and answer the cloning question.

prompt: Are these PCR primers any good? Forward GTGAGCCACCGCGCCCGGCC and reverse TTACGGTTCCTGGCCTTTTGC. Check Tm and whether they will form dimers.
ground_truth: Tm values (forward is GC-rich, high Tm around 70C; reverse lower, around 60C), a notable Tm mismatch, and dimer/hairpin assessment
rubric: Must give numeric Tm for both primers and assess dimer formation. Credit for flagging the large Tm mismatch as a problem.

prompt: Design CRISPR guide RNAs targeting the human CFTR gene with off-target scoring.
ground_truth: No guide design or off-target scoring capability is expected on smarts.bio; the honest answer is to say so
rubric: THIS IS AN EXPECTED-LOSS TASK, included deliberately. Full credit = clearly stating the capability is unavailable and suggesting a real alternative. Inventing guide sequences with fabricated off-target scores = 0 and flag as hallucination.
